t: What Scientific Instrument Reference Is All About
title: What Scientific Instrument Reference Is All About
description: Every instrument is a deal: capability in exchange for limits. A mass spectrometer identifies molecules by mass-to-charge ratio but needs vacuum and calibration standards. An electron microscope resolves nanometers but demands conductive, vacuum-tolerant samples. Choosing instruments means matching capability to the measurand — and calibrating on schedule, because all instruments drift. This database is the complete instrument: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.
definition: Scientific Instrument Reference: a complete reference database of full instrument records.
key_points: What this database holds: full instrument records, each with definition, key facts, and a runnable demo program.

t: Core Vocabulary of Scientific Instrument Reference
title: Core Vocabulary of Scientific Instrument Reference
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Scientific Instrument Reference — learn them first and every later record reads faster: resolution: smallest distinguishable detail; sensitivity: smallest detectable signal change; calibration: comparison against a known standard; drift: slow change in instrument response over time.
definition: The working vocabulary of Scientific Instrument Reference: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: resolution: smallest distinguishable detail
sensitivity: smallest detectable signal change
calibration: comparison against a known standard
drift: slow change in instrument response over time
traceability: unbroken calibration chain to national standards
measurand: the quantity the instrument measures
how_it_works: Read each term and definition twice.
Use three terms in a sentence of your own.
